original_question: Characterize the global domain DMA(X, omega) of definition of the complex Monge-Ampere operator on a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega).
target_in_paper: Question 5 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi) in §1.1.3, 'Compact Kähler manifolds': 'Characterize DMA(X, ω).'
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem in the paper almost verbatim: it asks for a characterization of DMA(X, ω), the global domain of definition of the complex Monge-Ampère operator, on a compact Kähler manifold (X, ω).
missing_details: The ambient class should be named explicitly: the variable ranges over PSH(X, ω), the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions on a compact Kähler manifold (X, ω) of complex dimension n.

DMA(X, ω) should be defined exactly as in Definition 1.3: φ ∈ DMA(X, ω) means there exists a Radon measure μ such that for every sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C∞(X) decreasing to φ on X, the measures (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converge weakly to μ.
The quantifier 'for every decreasing smooth ω-psh approximating sequence' is essential; existence of only one good approximation sequence is not the definition used in the paper.
The operator being discussed should be written explicitly as the global complex Monge-Ampère operator φ ↦ (ω + dd^cφ)^n.
To make the question stand-alone, it should distinguish the global domain DMA(X, ω) from the local domain DMAloc(X, ω), which is separately defined in Definition 1.4.
The task should be stated as a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of membership in DMA(X, ω), not merely a request for examples, obstructions, or partial inclusions.
refined_question: Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let PSH(X, ω) denote the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions. For φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), say that φ belongs to DMA(X, ω) if there exists a Radon measure μ on X such that, for every sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C∞(X) decreasing to φ on X, the measures (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converge weakly to μ; in that case one writes (ω + dd^cφ)^n := μ. Characterize the class DMA(X, ω), i.e. give necessary and sufficient conditions for an ω-psh function on a compact Kähler manifold to belong to the global domain of definition of the complex Monge-Ampère operator.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, characterize those φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) for which the same weak-limit property holds when one replaces smooth ω-psh approximants by arbitrary bounded ω-psh approximants decreasing to φ; in particular, one may test this using the canonical truncations φ_j = max(φ, -j).
justification: The draft is aiming directly at Question 5 in §1.1.3. The paper first defines DMA(X, ω) in Definition 1.3 via weak convergence of (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n along every decreasing smooth ω-psh approximation, then immediately defines the local counterpart DMAloc(X, ω) in Definition 1.4 and stresses that the global and local domains are different. The official open problem is then stated exactly as 'Characterize DMA(X, ω).' The nearby discussion supplies the intended scope: DMA(X, ω) is a strict subclass of PSH(X, ω); Lelong numbers give an obstruction to membership; and the known subclasses E(X, ω) and DMAloc(X, ω) are both contained in DMA(X, ω). So your draft has the right target, but it needs the paper’s own definition of DMA(X, ω), the universal approximation quantifier, and the explicit global-vs-local distinction to be fully stand-alone and faithful.
